title: Metadata
summary: AEM turns each page's Metadata table and the site's bulk metadata sheets into the <title>, description, canonical and social tags in the head. Search engines, AI agents and link previews read these, not the page body.

items.title: One Metadata table
items.detail: Add a single Metadata table per page, by convention at the bottom of the document.

items.title: Page title
items.detail: Set title or rely on the first H1; it fills <title>, og:title and twitter:title.

items.title: Description
items.detail: Write a description; otherwise AEM uses the first paragraph with 10 or more words.

items.title: Share image
items.detail: Set image, or add /default-meta-image.png so every page unfurls with a proper image.

items.title: Canonical on prod host
items.detail: Set cdn.prod.host so AEM generates canonical URLs on your production domain.

items.title: Site-wide suffixes
items.detail: Put repeated properties like title:suffix and html-lang in the bulk metadata sheet, not on every page.

items.title: Bulk sheet order
items.detail: List the /** row first in the metadata sheet, then the more specific URL patterns.

items.title: Page overrides sparingly
items.detail: Use the page Metadata block for exceptions only; it always wins over bulk metadata.

items.title: Sheet published
items.detail: Preview and publish the metadata sheet after every change, or the site will not see it.

title: Redirects
summary: EDS serves 301 redirects from a redirects sheet in the content root, previewed and published like any page. Moving or retiring content without them loses visitors and search ranking.

items.title: Redirects sheet
items.detail: Keep a redirects sheet in the content root with Source and Destination columns.

items.title: Relative sources
items.detail: Write Source as a path only; use a full URL as Destination only for other sites.

items.title: helix-default sheet
items.detail: If the workbook has several sheets, keep the live rules on the sheet named helix-default.

items.title: Tested on preview
items.detail: Preview the sheet and check each redirect on .aem.page before publishing it.

items.title: Redirects hide pages
items.detail: A redirect wins over an existing page at the same URL, so remove stale rules.

items.title: Top URLs mapped
items.detail: Map popular legacy URLs and top backlinks 1-to-1 to their new pages.

items.title: Patterns at the CDN
items.detail: Put pattern rules, like dropping .html, at the CDN; the redirects sheet has no wildcards.

items.title: No homepage dumping
items.detail: Do not send pruned URLs to one common page such as the homepage.

items.title: 404s watched
items.detail: After go-live, watch 404s in Operational Telemetry and add the missing redirects.

title: Sitemap
summary: AEM generates sitemap.xml from published pages or from query indexes and a sitemap config, including hreflang for multilingual sites. It is how search engines find new and changed content.

items.title: Sitemap served
items.detail: Check /sitemap.xml (or your sitemap index) on the production domain lists the published pages.

items.title: Production URLs
items.detail: Set cdn.prod.host or an origin so sitemap URLs use your production domain.

items.title: noindex pages out
items.detail: Keep a robots column in the index so pages with noindex drop out of the sitemap.

items.title: Within limits
items.detail: Keep each sitemap under 50,000 URLs and 50MB uncompressed; split by section or language.

items.title: lastmod dates
items.detail: Add lastmod with a date format so crawlers can see when pages changed.

items.title: hreflang alternates
items.detail: On multilingual sites, configure languages with hreflang and alternate paths.

items.title: Generated index
items.detail: Add an index list so AEM builds /sitemap-index.xml, and delete any static copy in the repo.

items.title: Linked from robots.txt
items.detail: Reference the sitemap or sitemap index from robots.txt on the production domain.

items.title: Search Console
items.detail: Submit the sitemap in Google Search Console and watch coverage for weeks after launch.

title: Query index
summary: The query index is a JSON list of published pages and chosen properties, served at /query-index.json by default. Blogs, lists, feeds, search and the sitemap all build on it.

items.title: Index configured
items.detail: Create the index with the Index Admin tool or the Admin API index config.

items.title: Scoped paths
items.detail: Use include and exclude paths so only real pages land in the index.

items.title: Only needed fields
items.detail: Extract only the properties your lists use, such as title, image and description.

items.title: robots indexed
items.detail: Index the robots property so the sitemap and lists can skip noindex pages.

items.title: Selectors on source
items.detail: Write selectors against View Source HTML, not the decorated DOM.

items.title: Tested locally
items.detail: Run aem up --print-index and check every property extracts a value.

items.title: Reindexed
items.detail: Reindex after changing properties; otherwise pages update only when published.

items.title: Page record checked
items.detail: Check a page's record with the Admin API index endpoint and the Log Viewer.

items.title: Removed by unpublish
items.detail: Unpublish a page to take it out of the live index.

title: Indexing & robots
summary: EDS keeps *.aem.page and *.aem.live out of search, and lets your production domain be crawled through robots.txt and per-page robots metadata. Getting this wrong hides the site or leaks duplicates.

items.title: Platform domains blocked
items.detail: Leave .aem.page and .aem.live blocked; they send X-Robots-Tag noindex, nofollow by default.

items.title: Header gone on prod
items.detail: After go-live, confirm the production domain no longer sends X-Robots-Tag.

items.title: Production robots.txt
items.detail: Check production /robots.txt allows crawling and names your sitemap.

items.title: Custom robots.txt
items.detail: Edit a custom robots.txt in the robots.txt Editor or via the Admin API.

items.title: noindex, not Disallow
items.detail: To drop a page from search, allow crawling and set robots noindex; Disallow prevents that.

items.title: Page exceptions
items.detail: Add a robots row to one page's Metadata block for one-offs like thank-you pages.

items.title: Sections via bulk
items.detail: Set robots noindex for whole sections, such as /drafts/**, in the bulk metadata sheet.

items.title: Canonicals return 200
items.detail: Point canonical URLs at pages that return 2xx, never a redirect or a 404.

title: Site configuration
summary: The configuration service holds a site's code and content location, CDN, access, headers, index, sitemap and robots settings, managed via tools.aem.live or the Admin API. It replaces fstab.yaml and .helix sheets and enables repoless sites.

items.title: Config service in use
items.detail: Manage settings in the configuration service, not .helix/config sheets.

items.title: Code and content set
items.detail: Set the code owner and repo and the content source URL for the site.

items.title: No live switches
items.detail: Never change code or content location of a live site; create a new site and move the CDN origin.

items.title: Production CDN
items.detail: Set the cdn.prod host so canonicals and sitemaps use your real domain.

items.title: Roles granted
items.detail: Grant roles such as config and publish to named users in the access settings.

items.title: No secrets in public
items.detail: Keep secrets out of public config; anyone can read it at /config.json.

items.title: Legacy files removed
items.detail: Remove fstab.yaml, robots.txt, helix-query.yaml and helix-sitemap.yaml from the repo.

items.title: Canonical repoless site
items.detail: For repoless, keep one site whose org/site matches the GitHub owner/repo.

items.title: Versions to restore
items.detail: Use the Admin API config versions list to roll back a bad config change.

title: Site authentication
summary: Site authentication puts token-based protection on preview (aem.page), live (aem.live) or both. Use it for intranets or unreleased work, then make sure the CDN, authors and tooling can still get through.

items.title: Scope chosen
items.detail: Pick access/preview, access/live or access/site; protecting live locks out every visitor.

items.title: Site token, not admin
items.detail: Create a site token via the secrets endpoint; never use your Admin API token for site access.

items.title: GET before POST
items.detail: GET the access object before changing it, since each POST overwrites it.

items.title: 401 without token
items.detail: Confirm a plain request gets 401 and one with the token in Authorization succeeds.

items.title: CDN sends token
items.detail: Configure the CDN to add the Authorization header to every origin request.

items.title: Browser users
items.detail: Give people who browse the protected site a role, and have them sign in with AEM Sidekick.

items.title: Known limits
items.detail: Auth covers the whole site only: no per-path authorization and no custom denied page.

items.title: No wildcard CORS
items.detail: Avoid access-control-allow-origin * on protected sites; it exposes signed-in authors to CSRF.

items.title: Keys rotated
items.detail: Store API key values safely and rotate keys before they expire; they cannot be retrieved again.
